questions.statement: Choose the correct verb forms for this mixed conditional.
questions.context:
**Sentence:**
"If I _______ harder when I was young, I _______ a better job now."
questions.explanation:
**English:** This is a **mixed conditional** (3rd + 2nd): past unreal condition → present unreal result. "Had studied" (past perfect) + "would have" (present conditional).
*Español: Este es un condicional mixto: condición irreal pasada → resultado irreal presente.*

questions.subject: ingles

questions.context:
**Sentence:**
"_______ had I finished the exam when the fire alarm went off."
questions.explanation:
**English:** **Hardly... when** is an inversion structure meaning "as soon as" or "just." The structure requires auxiliary inversion: "Hardly had I..."
*Español: **Hardly... when** es una estructura de inversión que significa "apenas".*

questions.context:
**Formal statement:**
"The committee recommends that every student _______ the workshop."
questions.explanation:
**English:** After verbs like "recommend," "suggest," "insist," we use the **subjunctive** (base form without -s). This is formal English grammar.
*Español: Después de verbos como "recomendar", usamos el **subjuntivo** (forma base sin -s).*

questions.statement: Choose the correct cleft sentence structure.
questions.context:
**Original:** "Maria solved the problem."
**Emphasis on Maria:**

options.text: Maria was who solved the problem.
It was Maria who solved the problem.
What Maria solved was the problem.

questions.explanation:
**English:** **It was... who** is a cleft sentence that emphasizes the subject. This structure is common in formal and academic English.
*Español: **It was... who** es una oración hendida que enfatiza el sujeto.*

questions.subject: ingles

questions.context:
**Two sentences:**
"The students completed the project. They celebrated their success."

options.text: The students completed the project and celebrated.
Having completed the project, the students celebrated their success.
The students, completing the project, celebrated.
Completed the project, the students celebrated.

questions.explanation:
**English:** **Having + past participle** creates a participle clause showing a completed action before the main clause. It's more sophisticated than simple coordination.
*Español: **Having + participio pasado** crea una cláusula participial mostrando una acción completada antes de la principal.*

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct reported speech transformation.
questions.context:
**Direct speech:**
"I will have finished the report by tomorrow," said the manager.

options.text: The manager said he will have finished the report by tomorrow.
The manager said he would finish the report by the next day.
The manager said he would have finished the report by the next day.
The manager said he has finished the report by the next day.

questions.explanation:
**English:** "Will have finished" (future perfect) becomes "**would have finished**" in reported speech. "Tomorrow" becomes "the next day."
*Español: El futuro perfecto se convierte en condicional perfecto en el discurso indirecto.*

questions.context:
**Dialogue:**
A: "Did you submit the application?"
B: "Yes, I _______."
questions.explanation:
**English:** In ellipsis, we use the auxiliary verb alone to avoid repetition. "Yes, I did" = "Yes, I submitted the application."
*Español: En la elipsis, usamos solo el verbo auxiliar para evitar repetición.*

questions.statement: Choose the reduced relative clause version.
questions.context:
**Full sentence:**
"The book which was written by Orwell is a classic."

options.text: The book writing by Orwell is a classic.
The book written by Orwell is a classic.
The book which writing by Orwell is a classic.
The book was written by Orwell is a classic.

questions.explanation:
**English:** When reducing passive relative clauses, remove "which was" and keep the past participle: "written by Orwell."
*Español: Al reducir cláusulas relativas pasivas, eliminamos "which was" y mantenemos el participio pasado.*

questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: **Normal order:** "I have never seen such a beautiful sunset."

options.text: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
Never I have seen such a beautiful sunset.
I never have seen such a beautiful sunset.
Have I never seen such a beautiful sunset.

questions.explanation:
**English:** When fronting negative adverbs (never, rarely, seldom), we use **inversion**: "Never have I seen..."
*Español: Al poner adverbios negativos al principio, usamos inversión del auxiliar.*

questions.statement: Choose the best nominal clause to complete the sentence.
questions.context:
**Sentence:**
"_______ remains a mystery."

options.text: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation:
**English:** All options function as nominal clauses (noun phrases). **D is correct** because each can serve as the subject. "What caused her departure" is the most sophisticated.
*Español: Todas las opciones son cláusulas nominales válidas. La D es correcta.*

**Note:** The answer key marks C, but D ("All of the above") is technically more accurate. Accept both.
